key_insight: UltraQuant shows that 4-bit KV caching can preserve agent quality while dramatically improving latency and throughput in long-context, multi-turn workloads where cache pressure dominates.
engineering_relevance: The work is directly relevant to serving systems for context-heavy agents because it ties quantization choices to GPU residency, concurrency, and end-to-end response latency rather than cache compression alone.
method: Uses 4-bit KV-cache compression with TurboQuant-style rotation and codebook quantization as the quality anchor.
Adds practical robustness choices: asymmetric K/V treatment, Walsh-Hadamard rotation, QJL removal, and block-scale variants.
Implements an AMD GPU serving path with optimized decode-attention kernels and UltraQuant using FP8 queries, FP4 KV tensors, UE8M0 group scales, and native scaled-MFMA on CDNA4.
evidence_signal: On a long-context, multi-turn agentic workload, UltraQuant improved P50 time-to-first-token by 3.47x in the cache-pressured late rounds (2.3x overall) and increased output throughput by 1.63x versus the FP8 KV baseline.
watch_item: Results depend on specialized serving kernels and AMD CDNA4 hardware support, so portability and accuracy under different models or deployments may require re-tuning.
paper_title: UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents
